title: Statistics for any number
hints: The constraint allows `float64(x)` for every `T`, so do all the math in `float64`. Summing in `T` is the trap: `uint8` overflows at 255, and `x - mean` can't even be written in `T` because `mean` is a `float64`.

`Mean`: guard empty, then `sum += float64(x)` and divide by `float64(len(xs))`. `Variance`: get the mean, then `d := float64(x) - mean; sum += d * d`, divided by the count. `Median`: `sorted := slices.Clone(xs); slices.Sort(sorted)`.

Median: odd `n` → `float64(sorted[n/2])`; even → `(float64(sorted[n/2-1]) + float64(sorted[n/2])) / 2`. `Summarize`: call the three functions, and use `float64(slices.Min(xs))` / `float64(slices.Max(xs))` and `math.Sqrt(variance)`.
